answer: Operator-Bound Reputation Decay. Each identity carries a reputation score tied to its operator's verified off-chain credential, not its wallet. When a new wallet's activity correlates with an existing operator's cluster, the shared score decays and a plume of throttled rate limits spreads across all that operator's identities. The signal is the operator's credential, so cloning wallets gains nothing: each clone drags the operator's whole haven of scores down. An attacker must acquire and verify fresh operator credentials per clone, paying real KYC cost each time.
